Superyacht and luxury vessel documentation.

Vessel Documentation

Superyacht documentation requires a level of dimensional precision that consumer-grade tools don't deliver. We capture using professional LiDAR and photogrammetry instrumentation, producing point cloud data accurate enough for refit specification and engineering drawings. The navigable digital twin gives your wider team and your broker an accessible model of the vessel — the underlying point cloud data is what your refit yard actually works from. Alturascope produces structured condition documentation for luxury vessels: for charter marketing, pre-purchase diligence, refit planning, and the ongoing asset management that significant vessels require.

What we document.

Complete interior — saloons, cabins, galley, engine room access areas, deck spaces. Equipment and systems inventory. Condition of surfaces, fittings, and installed equipment. Areas accessible by conventional survey and those requiring specialist access techniques. The documentation captures the vessel as it exists, with the precision that high-value asset management demands.

What you receive.

Millimetre-accurate point cloud data from professional LiDAR capture, a navigable digital twin for your wider team and brokers, equipment and asset schedule formatted for refit specification, narrated walkthrough, conditions report, and labeled photo storyboard. All delivered through ScopeWalk and accessible to your management team, brokers, or refit yard as needed.

Who this is for.

Yacht brokers, charter operators, refit yards, yacht management companies, and private owners. Whether you need marketing documentation that shows the vessel at its best, a pre-purchase condition record, or a complete documentation package to support refit planning — the deliverable is structured for the decision you're making.

Frequently asked questions.

What does a full vessel documentation package include? +

A full vessel documentation package includes precision LiDAR point cloud data of all accessible interior spaces, a navigable digital twin for remote exploration, an equipment and asset schedule documenting installed systems and fittings, a narrated walkthrough with commentary on observed conditions and areas of note, a conditions report, and a labeled photo storyboard. The scope is tailored to the vessel and the purpose of the documentation — whether that's charter marketing, refit planning, or asset management.

How is yacht documentation used in refit planning? +

For refit planning, the point cloud data provides the dimensional accuracy that refit yards need for specification and engineering drawings. The navigable digital twin allows designers and yard teams to explore the vessel remotely and understand spatial constraints before work begins. The equipment schedule provides a complete inventory of installed systems formatted for specification work. The conditions report identifies areas requiring attention with prioritised findings. Together, these deliverables give the refit team a complete picture of the vessel without needing multiple on-board visits.

Can you document vessels anywhere in the US or Caribbean? +

Yes. We operate a national travel model across the US and can mobilise to any marina or shipyard location. For vessels in the Caribbean, we can arrange documentation visits by arrangement. Travel costs are included in project pricing — there are no surprise charges. Contact us with the vessel's location and we'll confirm logistics.

What is the difference between a marketing scan and a full documentation survey? +

A marketing scan focuses on presenting the vessel at its best for charter or brokerage purposes — the navigable digital twin serves as an immersive virtual tour that potential clients or buyers can explore. A full documentation survey goes further: it includes precision LiDAR capture for engineering-grade accuracy, a complete equipment inventory, a conditions assessment, above-deck and below-deck documentation, and a structured report. The purpose determines the scope.

How long does a full vessel documentation visit take? +

Duration depends on the vessel size and the scope of documentation required. A standard visit for a 30-40 metre vessel typically takes one full day on board. Larger vessels or more comprehensive documentation scopes may require two days. We confirm the schedule during the brief and coordinate with the vessel's crew or management team to ensure minimal disruption.
